fields.features_heading: Inside a Drag and Drop Quiz on Emergent
fields.features_subheading: Each question is a set of cards and the slots they go in. Emergent builds both, plus the scoring and a table of every placement.
fields.feature_1:
Four drag types from one prompt

Describe the question in plain words, such as five fractions to order. Emergent builds the cards, the drop zones, and the answer key, and a follow-up prompt changes any of them.
fields.feature_2:
Points for each card in its slot

Set the scoring rule: 1 point for every card in the right place, or nothing until all of them are. The app applies it when a taker submits, and the score shows on the next screen.
fields.feature_3:
A tap option beside every drag

Ask for a tap option, and Emergent builds it next to the drag: tap a card, then tap its slot. A taker who cannot drag on a small phone screen still finishes the same question.
fields.feature_4:
Every placement saved to your database

Each submission saves which card landed in which slot, in a database you own. Sort the rows by card, and the one placed wrong most often sits at the top, ready for the next lesson.
fields.feature_5:
Score emails and Slack alerts

The app emails each score to the taker and sends a Slack alert to the teacher when someone falls below the pass mark. Emergent puts no cap on responses, so a whole grade can play.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain and the full code

Host the quiz on a custom domain, which is included in Emergent and uses credits. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and keep the quiz after the term ends.

quiz_plan.promise: the quiz plays the page's promise: a drag and drop quiz maker a visitor can take, whose results answer what the H1 says it builds

plan.angle: The top 10 is quiz tools that describe a drag-and-drop editor (forms.app, Formly, Elfsight, Canva) or a list of quiz makers, and only the AI Overview names drag-and-drop question types. This page is about the questions themselves: order, sort, match and rank cards that the app scores card by card, with a tap alternative for anyone who cannot drag, and every placement saved to a database the builder owns. A playable quiz on the page helps the visitor pick the drag type that fits what they test.
tab_stories: Marisol Echeverry's 26 fourth graders at Abernook Elementary drag 5 fraction cards into order from smallest to largest, the app gives 1 point per card in the right slot, and 6 students put 1/3 before 1/4.

Varnhold Supply has each new warehouse hire sort 12 item cards into the 3 bins on its waste chart; 10 of 12 passes, a lower score means a retake and a Slack message to the shift supervisor, and 11 of 14 October hires passed on the first try.

Lintwhistle Language Center's 22 adult learners match 8 Spanish words to 8 pictures, every wrong pairing is saved, and 9 of 22 dropped the word for spoon on the fork picture, so Thursday's class opens with kitchen words.

Graymoss Roasters lets shoppers drag 5 flavor notes into ranked order, the note ranked first picks one of 3 roasts on the result screen, and 171 of 412 October shoppers put chocolate first and were shown the dark roast.
